speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty. To begin, how many weeks ago was your surgery performed?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. You mentioned shooting pain when eating and difficulty wearing earrings; does the pain also occur when you move your jaw or chew gum?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.
